newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 100,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 100,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 100,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender on Wednesday, the eighth of the new series for the 1996/97 crop, traders said.
This week's tonnage was unlikely to reach the 129,500 tonnes awarded in the EU's last tender on September 18, they said.
Currency movements were cited as one reason for the expected lower tonnage.
"I would think that with the dollar having come off it might not get to the 100,000 (tonnes) level today," a trader said, forecasting between 80,000 and 100,000 tonnes.
But another gave a more conservative estimate of between 40,000 and 80,000 tonnes.
"We're not expecting a great deal -- the market is a bit lower, the dollar is weaker and there's not much (sugar) left for the October/November period," he said.
But traders agreed on the maximum restitution for licences this week and forecast 44.709 Ecus (European Currency Units) per 100 kg of sugar, after last week's 44.837 Ecus.
Export licences are valid from October to February.
